reader.requirement: A CLOSE naming several file-name-1 operands executes exactly as one separate CLOSE per file-name-1 in the written order, each with its own phrase, its own I-O status update and its own exception processing, so a failure on one file neither stops nor reorders the closes of the others.

edition-consulted.switches: close-with-lock-removed-2023 (COBOL0902): the WITH LOCK phrase compiles at 85 through 2014 and is refused at 2023
DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 1985 the physical file is locked, from 2002 the file connector
ec.Enabled(EC-REPORT-NOT-TERMINATED): the report-file raise after each implicit CLOSE, never enabled at 1985 (no exception checking); the per-file loop is the same

reader.edition-search: Grepped SequentialIoBinder.cs#BindClose and SequentialIoEmitter.cs#EmitClose for DialectLevel/DialectBehavior: the split into one BoundClose per file-name (BoundImplicitSeries) and the per-file close, status store and USE hook read no edition; the edition arms on the path are the WITH LOCK phrase's existence and what it locks.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the one-close-per-file series is the same at every edition; what differs on the path is only the WITH LOCK phrase (legal at 1985, refused at 2023) and its lock target, which are other rules
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf18_02 covers order across organizations and a USE procedure seeing the earlier closes done and the later not yet; not covered: a failing file in the middle with later files still closed, the same file named twice, mixed per-file phrases (WITH LOCK, REEL) (probe cl1)

reader.notes: BindClose builds one BoundClose per file-name-1 in source order inside a BoundImplicitSeries, and EmitClose closes, stores the FILE STATUS and runs the USE hook per file before the next, which is exactly the separate-statements reading. Probes cl1/cl2 show a failing middle file does not stop later closes and a repeated name behaves as a second CLOSE.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-121/src/clr1.cob (clr1-002) at --std 85, NO USE procedure anywhere and FILE STATUS on each file: CLOSE FA FB FC FD1 over sequential, sequential-not-open, relative and indexed files gave A=00 B=42 C=00 D=00 and every other file was really closed (reopen 00, records read back AAAA CCCC DDDD); the failing file last (CLOSE FD1 FC FA FB) and the same four as separate CLOSE statements both gave A=00 B=42 C=00 D=00: the multi-file form equals the separate statements also without a USE procedure and across organizations. The first compile (clr1-001) refused WRITE/READ of relative/indexed/sequential files without INVALID KEY/AT END and no USE (COBOL6826, §1985:VIII.4.9.3 SR3 etc.), a correct 1985 refusal unrelated to the rule. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.2.4 GR8.
